record.paper_title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem
record.original_question: For a positive integer n, what are necessary and sufficient conditions for a multiset Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_n} of real numbers to be exactly the spectrum of an n x n matrix that is both symmetric and entrywise nonnegative?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let Λ = {λ_1, λ_2, …, λ_n} be a multiset of real numbers. The Symmetric Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem asks: determine necessary and sufficient conditions on Λ so that there exists an n × n real matrix A satisfying

(i) A is symmetric (A = A^T),
(ii) every entry of A is nonnegative (A_{ij} ≥ 0 for all i, j), and
(iii) the spectrum of A, counted with multiplicity, equals Λ.

Give an explicit characterization, in terms of the numbers λ_1, …, λ_n alone, of those multisets Λ ⊂ ℝ that arise as the spectrum of some such symmetric entrywise-nonnegative n × n matrix.
artifact.status_search_result: The Symmetric Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem (SNIEP) is completely solved only for n ≤ 4 (where it coincides with the general real NIEP, by Johnson–Laffey–Loewy, 1996). For n = 5 partial results exist (e.g., Loewy–McDonald) and for general n ≥ 5 the problem remains open; only various sufficient conditions are known. A full characterization is widely regarded as a hard open problem.

status_evidence.title: A map of sufficient conditions for the symmetric nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of sufficient conditions; the SNIEP remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: SNIEP is open for general n; only sufficient conditions are known.

status_evidence.title: The symmetric nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem for 5 × 5 matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the 5x5 case, indicating the problem is unresolved beyond n=4.
status_evidence.claim: Problem solved fully only up to n=4; n=5 still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of sets realizable by compensation in the SNIEP
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work giving partial (sufficient) characterizations via compensation.
